content.comment_body: Hello, I installed [product_name] on my laptop using an older DVD. Over time, I updated this to [version_no]. Now I have a new laptop and am uncertain if and how the license can be moved to the new device. The new laptop does not have a DVD drive. I would appreciate any advice on how to proceed.

On your old or another computer, you can copy the entire CD/DVD to a USB stick. On the new device, install the software from the USB stick. Afterwards, you can perform an upgrade on the [company_name] website.

There is no separate license like with some other software (e.g., [product_name]). The installation of the full version of [product_name] acts as the license. If your old laptop is still operational, create an image of the CD/DVD and put it on a USB stick. You can download the latest version of [product_name] from the [company_name] website, but the download is subject to export restrictions. You will need to log in and register to access export-restricted software. Follow the instructions given in the relevant [company_name] FAQ for installing a downloaded upgrade of [product_name], whether or not an older version is already installed.
Thank you all. Your input is really useful. I’ll try the suggested method.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering difficulties relocating [product_name] to a new laptop mainly due to legacy physical media and unclear licensing requirements. The lack of DVD drives in newer laptops complicates installation from the original media, while confusion over license transfer and activation exists due to differences from other software by [company_name]. Community advice is valued, but manual transfer and web-based upgrade procedures present usability challenges.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks a straightforward method to transfer and activate [product_name] on a new device, hoping to avoid outdated hardware requirements and complicated license management.
